On August 17, The Financial Times reported that AI video startup Higgsfield raised $400 million at a $5.4 billion valuation from investors. It includes The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc. (NYSE:GS) and Intel Corporation (NASDAQ:INTC), as the two-year-old company pushes deeper into corporate marketing subscriptions. A Wall Street bank and a chipmaker in the middle of its own turnaround both chose to back the same AI video startup. That raises the real question: does this shared bet show real conviction in Higgsfield's business, or are two very different companies chasing the same hot trend for very different reasons? The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc. (NYSE:GS) invested through its Equity Growth fund, and the firm has estimated the global creator economy could grow from $250 billion in 2023 to $480 billion by 2027. Higgsfield's annualized revenue reached $700 million in August, up from just $20 million a year earlier, and the share of revenue coming from businesses rather than individual creators jumped from under 25% in January to a majority today. A $5.4 billion valuation for a two-year-old company is a significant bet on continued hypergrowth. Higgsfield's AI-generated marketing videos face real competitive and reputational risk given the technology has already "unsettled" parts of Hollywood over its effect on creative jobs. Backing Higgsfield gives Intel Corporation (NASDAQ:INTC) exposure to a fast-growing AI application layer beyond its core chip business. It is diversifying its AI-related bets at a time when Intel wants to show relevance across the AI stack, not just as a hardware supplier. Intel just raised $20 billion specifically to fund its own core semiconductor turnaround. Putting money into an unrelated AI video startup, even a fast-growing one, is a distraction from the capital-intensive turnaround Intel Corporation (NASDAQ:INTC)'s own shareholders care about most. The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc. (NYSE:GS) was held by 83 hedge funds as of Q1 2026, up from 78. Intel Corporation (NASDAQ:INTC) was held by 112, up from 96. Higgsfield's growth numbers are real. However, Goldman and Intel are backing it for very different strategic reasons, one purely financial, the other more about staying visible across the AI stack. title: Media Mondays schedule for GS Football announced - Grice Connect
content:
Fans of Georgia Southern football will have three opportunities each Monday during the season to get the latest on the program thanks to initiatives led by GATA Productions.

Starting on Monday, Aug. 31, Inside Georgia Southern Football with Clay Helton will be broadcast live on ESPN+ from 11:30 a.m. to noon (ET). It will also be shown locally on WJCL in Savannah on Saturdays at 11:30 a.m. (ET). The 30-minute show, hosted by "Voice of the Eagles" Danny Reed, will feature segments with Coach Helton reviewing the previous week and previewing the upcoming matchup. Whitney Haworth will also be on site for a special guest interview each week giving fans of Eagle Nation a look into members of the football team and coaching staff.

At 12:30 p.m. (ET), Coach Helton and two players will talk to the media for their weekly press conference. This too, will be aired live on ESPN+ and should last approximately 30 minutes.

Finally, Hail Southern Live returns to Wild Wing Cafe in Statesboro and also debuts on Aug. 31 at 7 p.m. (ET). The one-hour show will be carried on the Georgia Southern Sports Network, Georgia Southern Athletics Facebook Live, YouTube Live and GSEagles.com. Each Monday throughout the season, Coach Helton will join the show along with an Eagle football standout and a spotlight on Georgia Southern's Olympic sports. Fans can tweet @GSSportsNetwork with their questions for the show or submit on the Facebook Live feed. Hail Southern Live also airs on 94.9 FM, the flagship radio station of GS Athelics, as well as the Varsity Network.

Located off Highway 67 on the corner of Fair Road and Aspen Heights Drive, Wild Wing Cafe originally opened in Statesboro in 2014.

Georgia Southern also officially announced its football radio crew for the 2026 season. Led by new Voice of the Eagles, Adam Young, this veteran group will call all the action on the Georgia Southern Sports Network, along with provide content on various social media platforms. Young is in his first year with the Eagles, but is no stranger to the booth. Young arrives in Statesboro after serving as the Director of Broadcasting and play-by-play voice at New Mexico State, where he called football, basketball, baseball and numerous other sports while overseeing the Aggies' broadcasting operation and multimedia content.

Joining him in the booth will be local media legend Frank Sulkowski, who makes the move up from the sidelines to the color analyst role. The host of WJCL's Morning Show and former sports director at WJCL, Sulkowski has received several awards, from the Georgia Association of Broadcasters GABBY, the Georgia Associate Press as well as being named the Connect Savannah Readers Choice for best Sportscaster for eight years in a row. He has also been recognized by the Special Olympics of Georgia for Outstanding Media Coverage.

Jeff Roberts, former sports director at WTOC, will join the team as the sideline reporter. He has also worked with the Savannah Ghost Pirates and with radio and television networks in Michigan.

title: Karol G Viajando Por El Mundo Tropitour: The Complete US Stadium Guide - Event Tickets Center

The Viajando Por El Mundo Tropitour is Karol G's biggest undertaking yet: a 60-plus-date global stadium run that launched July 24 at Soldier Field in Chicago and stretches across North America, Latin America, and Europe through July 2027. The Karol G tour makes her the first Latina artist to headline a global stadium tour at this scale, and she is also the first Latina to headline Coachella. This guide covers every remaining US date, the rotating openers, what the show looks like, and what to expect at each venue. Buy Karol G Tropitour tickets at Event Tickets Center to lock in your seats for any remaining stops. Karol G has nine remaining US stadium stops on the books, with three cities hosting back-to-back nights. Here's the full remaining schedule, with every show kicking off at 7:00 p.m. local time. Becky G joins Karol G for 10 select dates on the North American leg, though she isn't on every stop. Elena Rose and Greeicy also appear as support depending on the city. There's no single fixed opener for the tour, so it's worth checking the listing for your specific date before you plan around a particular guest. Tropicoqueta, released June 20, 2025, on Bichota Records and Interscope, is Karol G's fourth consecutive No. 1 on Billboard's Top Latin Albums chart and earned a Grammy nomination for Best Latin Pop Album. It features collaborations with Marco Antonio Solís, Feid, Manu Chao, and Greeicy, weaving Tropicoqueta into a set that still leans on classic Karol G songs from her back catalog. While the 2023 Mañana Será Bonito tour filled arenas, the Tropitour scales that same show up in full stadiums. The Tropitour is built around elaborate staging, pyrotechnics, costume changes, and moments designed to pull the crowd into the performance. It's built for stadiums seating 60,000 to 82,000, and early reports from the tour's launch at Soldier Field point to a visual style that carries over from her Coachella 2026 headlining set. Expect a show built around scale rather than one built around surprises. Based on early stops on the tour, a Karol G concert runs about two hours to two hours and 15 minutes. Doors typically open around 90 minutes before the 7:00 p.m. showtime at most venues, though that can shift by city. Treat these numbers as a solid reference point rather than a guarantee, since the runtime depends on the night's openers and how much time Karol G spends interacting with the crowd. Here's the fullest confirmed setlist so far, pulled from the tour's opening shows in Chicago. Each remaining stop has its own quirks worth knowing before you go. Here's what to expect at every venue on the rest of the US run. The Alamodome seats up to 77,000 for concerts and sits just east of downtown San Antonio, within walking distance of the River Walk. On-site lots surround the venue, though rideshare pickup near the Durango Street side tends to move faster on show nights. Standard clear-bag policies apply, so leave oversized bags behind. Sun Bowl Stadium sits on the UTEP campus, and most fans park in the surrounding campus lots or take a short ride-share from downtown El Paso. At 51,500 seats, it's the smallest venue on this leg of the tour, so arriving early is worth it if you're in general admission. Clear-bag policies are standard here as well. Gillette Stadium, home to the Patriots and Revolution, holds about 66,829 for concerts and offers direct MBTA commuter rail service from Boston on event days. On-site parking lots fill up fast, so anyone without a rideshare plan should budget extra time. The stadium enforces a clear-bag policy at all gates. MetLife Stadium is one of the largest venues on the remaining US run at 90,000 seats, and NJ Transit's rail line runs directly to the stadium from New York Penn Station on show days. On-site parking is available but sells out for high-demand shows, so booking ahead helps. Expect the same clear-bag standard used across NFL venues. Mercedes-Benz Stadium sits in downtown Atlanta, within walking distance of MARTA's Vine City and GWCC/CNN Center stations. The venue holds roughly 83,000 for concerts and is known for a strict clear-bag policy enforced at every entrance. Parking decks surround the stadium, though rates climb closer to showtime. Reliant Stadium, formerly NRG Stadium, holds about 72,220 for concerts and anchors Houston's NRG Park complex, which includes its own dedicated parking lots. METRORail's Red Line stops nearby, offering an alternative to driving. Bag policies follow the standard clear-bag format used at most NFL stadiums. Hard Rock Stadium seats around 65,326 for concerts and sits north of downtown Miami in Miami Gardens, so budgeting extra drive time or rideshare surge pricing is worth planning for. On-site parking lots are the most reliable option since public transit access is limited. The venue enforces a clear-bag policy at all gates. Raymond James Stadium holds about 75,000 and sits a short drive from downtown Tampa, with several official lots on-site for parking. Rideshare drop-off near the main gates tends to move faster than the general lots on busy nights. Standard clear-bag rules apply. AT&T Stadium is the largest stop on the tour at 105,000 seats, located in Arlington between Dallas and Fort Worth. Parking is spread across multiple official lots, and pre-booking a spot is worth it given the venue's size and the volume of a stadium show. title: GS The Fresh achieves 500 franchise stores milestone - Mobility Plaza
content: The South Korean supermarket chain has surpassed 500 franchised locations, strengthening its neighborhood grocery model through franchise expansion, quick commerce and data-driven operations. GS The Fresh has opened its 500th franchised supermarket, becoming the first player in South Korea’s supermarket sector to reach the milestone as it continues to expand its franchise-led growth strategy. The new store opened in Seoul’s Songpa district and brings the retailer’s total store count to 603 locations nationwide. The outlet has been designed to serve nearby residential communities, targeting families and young couples with everyday grocery shopping needs. Operated by GS Retail, GS The Fresh traces its origins to Lucky Super Chain, established in 1974. The company said it currently welcomes around 150 million customer visits annually and remains the leading supermarket operator in South Korea based on store count, sales and operating profit. The retailer attributes much of its growth to a shift from a company-owned model toward a franchise-focused structure, drawing on decades of experience from convenience chain GS25. Following increased demand for neighborhood shopping during and after the pandemic, the franchise model enabled the company to accelerate store openings and expand into more local communities. According to GS Retail, franchised stores now account for approximately 83% of the GS The Fresh network, up from just over 50% in 2020 after the company expanded its chain operation model. Under this system, product assortment, merchandising and ordering processes are standardized and supported centrally, allowing store owners to focus more on local marketing and customer engagement. The company is also increasing investment in quick commerce as an additional growth driver for franchisees. Through its Woori Neighborhood GS app and partnerships with delivery platforms including Baemin, Coupang Eats, Yogiyo and Naver Shopping, GS The Fresh offers grocery deliveries within one hour from most stores nationwide.

There’s a new resident on the Georgia Southern University campus, housed inside the Allen E. Paulson College of Engineering and Computing: A humanoid robot designed to serve as a cornerstone for advanced research and applied, hands-on classroom learning for students. According to a release from Georgia Southern, the robot expands robotics and artificial intelligence initiatives. Unlike traditional industrial robots, the platform is designed to interact in human environments, giving students and faculty opportunities to study human-robot interaction, machine learning and autonomous navigation, the release stated. “This is more than just a piece of equipment; it is a catalyst for innovation at Georgia Southern,” said Rami Haddad, Ph.D., former interim dean of the Paulson College of Engineering and chair of the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering. Students across multiple disciplines, including computer science, mechanical engineering, electrical engineering and information technology, will collaborate on programming, maintaining and optimizing the platform. “By integrating this humanoid robot into our classrooms and research laboratories, we are giving students hands-on experience with the technologies that are transforming engineering, computing and industry across the world,” Haddad said. The capabilities position Georgia Southern graduates to help meet the growing demand for talent at the region’s logistics centers, automated ports and advanced manufacturing facilities, the release stated. “Investments in advanced technologies like this humanoid robot reinforce Georgia Southern’s commitment to preparing students for the future of work while strengthening the university’s impact on the region,” said Avinandan Mukherjee, Ph.D., provost and executive vice president for Academic Affairs. The robot will be housed in a specialized, multidisciplinary laboratory that will serve as a shared resource for undergraduate projects, master’s theses and faculty-led research. “Our new robot will enhance interdisciplinary research, strengthen experiential learning and equip our graduates with the knowledge and expertise needed to lead in the rapidly evolving fields of robotics, automation and artificial intelligence,” said Abhijit Bhattacharyya, Ph.D., dean of the College of Engineering and Computing. The campus community may also catch a glimpse of the robot going to class, working in the labs and walking around campus.

title: Vikings Sign Cornerback Tre Hawkins - Minnesota Vikings
content:
EAGAN, Minn. — The Vikings on Tuesday signed cornerback Tre Hawkins ahead of closing the 2026 preseason at the Denver Broncos on Friday. In a corresponding roster move, the Vikings waived cornerback Dwight McGlothern, Jr., with an injury designation. Larry Hawkins III, who goes by Tre, was selected 209th overall in the 2023 NFL Draft by the Giants, with whom he spent his first two pro seasons. He played in all 17 games as a rookie, recording 35 tackles. In 2024, he logged his first career interception when he picked off New Orleans' Derek Carr — snapping New York's 11-game stretch without an interception. Hawkins was waived during final roster cuts prior to the 2025 campaign and worked out with multiple teams before joining Washington's practice squad and signing a futures deal. He suffered a hamstring injury, however, and was waived by the Commanders. Hawkins played two seasons at Old Dominion after transferring from Trinity Valley (2018-19). During his senior season for the Monarchs, he started all 12 games and ranked fourth on the team with 57 tackles. He added two interceptions, six pass breakups and three fumble recoveries, which tied for the Sun Belt lead. At Old Dominion's Pro Day, Hawkins impressed with a time of 4.39 seconds in the 40-yard dash. A Texas native, Hawkins played at Temple High School and racked up 60 tackles, two interceptions and seven pass breakups as a senior. McGlothern initially joined Minnesota as an undrafted free agent in 2024. He has spent time on the practice squad and 53-man roster over the past two seasons, appearing in 15 games. title: The 2027 Corvette GS Out-Grips The Z06 And The ZR1, But An Old C7 GS Out-Brakes It - Carscoops
content:
The new car needs 144 feet to brake from 70 mph, or 21 feet further than the old C7 Grand Sport The new Chevy Corvette Grand Sport has the potential to become one of the most popular C8 models, and based on a recent performance test by Car and Driver, it sits perfectly between the entry-level Stingray and the screaming Z06. It has all the right ingredients to be a hit. The 2027 Chevy Corvette GS tested here was a $142,380 3LT fitted with the $20,695 Z52 Track Performance package and $10,995 carbon-fiber wheels. Much like the 2027 Corvette Stingray, the Grand Sport has debuted with GM’s new sixth-generation LS6 small-block, a 6.7-liter naturally aspirated V8, rather than the outgoing LT2 6.2-liter unit. In both the Stingray and Grand Sport, this engine delivers 535 hp and 520 lb-ft (705 Nm) of torque, gains of 40 hp and 50 lb-ft (68 Nm). Read: 35% Of 2027 Corvettes Built So Far Are The Pricier Grand Sport With an eight-speed dual-clutch transmission, rear-wheel drive, and the same 5.56:1 final-drive ratio as the Z06, Car and Driver set a 0-60 mph time in the Grand Sport in 2.7 seconds with a one-foot rollout, or 2.9 seconds without it. Reaching 100 mph (161 km/h) took 6.8 seconds, while the quarter-mile came in 11.0 seconds, at 123 mph (198 km/h). This conveniently places the GS right between the old 6.2-liter Stingray with its 11.2-second quarter-mile at 122 mph and the 10.5-second set by a Z06 at 131 mph. In addition, the GS’s run to 60 mph sits perfectly between the 2.8 seconds of the old Stingray and the 2.6 seconds of the Z06. The publication has yet to test the 2027 Stingray with the 6.7-liter engine, but it should deliver times roughly the same as the Grand Sport. It’s on the skidpan where the new Grand Sport really stands out from other C8 models. Clad in Michelin Pilot Sport Cup 2R tires, it posted a peak of 1.18 g, above the Z06 at 1.16 g, ZR1X at 1.14 g, and the ZR1 at 1.13 g. Braking from 70 mph to a standstill took 144 feet, slightly longer than the ZR1X’s 135 feet, and actually well behind the decade-old C7 Corvette Grand Sport Z07, which managed the same 1.18 g of maximum cornering grip but needed just 123 feet to stop from 70 mph. title: Lunchbreak: The Athletic Predicts Win Totals; Randy Moss Recognized for Fantasy Football Prowess - Minnesota Vikings
content: Win projections can go out the door in a few weeks, but until then they're at least interesting. The Athletic's Austin Mock recently revealed his regular-season team win projections, and on Wednesday the publication's "experts" weighed in to determine the accuracy of Mock's model. Are the calculations too high, too low or right on the nose? You can find analysis for all 32 clubs here. Now, let's peek at Minnesota and Alec Lewis' verdict. Mock projected 8.7 wins for the Vikings, which according to Lewis is just right. Lewis wrote why there's an opportunity to surpass that figure: You can make reasonable arguments on both sides of this one. On the positive end, the Vikings present upside. Quarterback Kyler Murray's floor should far exceed the play from 2025, and his dual-threat ability could further unlock advantages. Additionally, the Vikings revamped their run game with the hiring of Assistant Head Coach Frank Smith (and promotion of offensive line coach Keith Carter). Increase the offensive output, and Minnesota could vie for the NFC North. View photos of Vikings players during Training Camp practice on August 24 at TCO Performance Center. Conversely, Lewis pointed out the negative potential due to relying on youth and needing depth: A negative view is valid, too. The Vikings defense is banking heavily on Defensive Coordinator Brian Flores, the scheme's ability to create chaos and a bevy of young players at all spots. Take a step back defensively — and suffer injuries on the offensive line or at quarterback — and the Vikings could find themselves in a rough spot. So you're aware, here's the number of wins that Mock projected, plus beat writers' verdicts, for the rest of the division: Chicago 9.6 (just right); Detroit 10.2 (just right); and Green Bay 9.7 (just right). View the best photos of Vikings legend and Pro Football Hall of Famer Randy Moss. Last week, Randy Moss returned to the franchise where his iconic NFL career began, and his presence was felt and appreciated — in Vikings offensive meetings and on the sidelines at practice and U.S. Bank Stadium when Minnesota hosted Baltimore in the second week of the preseason. Moss' aura, still, reigned supreme on the grass. Of course it did. He's one of the best to ever do it. He's still gaining recognition, too. Moss on Monday was honored as one of the first two members in the ESPN Fantasy Football Hall of Fame during a special segment of the Fantasy Football Marathon. The new fraternity acknowledges the best players and most memorable moments since fantasy football started on ESPN.com in 1995. Moss was inducted to the "Players Wing" and former Chiefs RB Jamaal Charles was selected as the first recipient in the "Moments Wing" for the 59.5 fantasy points that he scored Dec. 15, 2013, in Week 15 against the Raiders. Charles' performance featured eight rushes for 20 yards and a touchdown and eight receptions for 195 yards and four touchdowns. Moss was chosen for the entirety of his career, which included 15,292 receiving yards and 157 total touchdowns. Those numbers amounted to 3,467.34 career fantasy points. Here's what ESPN wrote: One of the most physically dominant wide receivers, Moss routinely beat opposing defenders by using his speed, size and jumping ability — yeah, he "Mossed" them. He excelled right from the start: His 304.7 fantasy points and 17 receiving touchdowns in 1998 remain rookie wide receiver records. Moss was a top-six positional performer in each of his first six seasons (and eight in total), and he set the NFL's single-season receiving touchdowns record with 23 in 2007 (on the Patriots), a year in which he finished with 385.3 fantasy points, which was the second most ever by a WR at that time. His 50 career games of 25-plus fantasy points trail only Jerry Rice among wide receivers. Moss recorded a short video to thank ESPN for the distinction when he visited TCO Performance Center last week. He expressed his gratitude with his signature personality showing through, and in front of the Vikings Ring of Honor player plaques lining a wall near the staff entrance of the building. "The first player to ever? That means I did something right and broke a few records," Moss quipped. Click here to check out the full article and watch the video Moss sent to ESPN. title: Why Did Banking Stocks GS, JPM, BAC Surge To 52-Week Highs Today? - Stocktwits
content: Shares of Goldman Sachs Group, Inc. (GS), JPMorgan Chase & Co. (JPM), and Bank of America Corp. (BAC) surged to annual highs after the banks posted stellar second-quarter earnings results that beat market expectations. GS stock led the climb among banking stocks, surging more than 9% after its record Q2 results triggered a buy-in. JPM stock rose 2.5% after its results surged past Wall Street expectations, while BAC stock also soared nearly 2% to a record high. GS stock climbed to a record high of $1,143.84 on Tuesday after the company reported record Q2 results that tore past analysts’ expectations. Goldman Sachs posted quarterly revenue of $20.98 billion, significantly higher than Wall Street's $16.4 billion estimate, according to Koyfin data. The investment bank also reported earnings of $15.91 per share, ahead of the $14.40 consensus estimate, while net income reached a record $6.32 billion for the quarter. The strong results were fueled by robust performance in investment banking, equities trading, and asset management, as companies continued to tap capital markets and pursue AI-related financing and strategic deals. "There's a lot of capital out there," CEO David Solomon said in an interview with CNBC on Tuesday. "I'm not concerned about the ability for the capital to be available for things that make sense." GS stock has surged nearly 25% so far this year. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment was ‘extremely bullish’ at the time of writing. JPM stock climbed to a 52-week high of $344.73 on Tuesday, driven by strong Q2 results that boosted investor interest in the company. The bank posted revenue of $57.35 billion versus a consensus estimate of $51.3 billion, while earnings per share (EPS) came in at $7.70 per share versus an expectation of $ 5.80 per share, based on Fiscal.ai data. JPMorgan delivered its strongest trading quarter on record, with trading revenue jumping 35% year over year to $12.1 billion. CEO Jamie Dimon said every business segment achieved record results, noting that market conditions remain favorable for sustained activity. Investment banking fees climbed 30% from a year earlier to $3.3 billion, marking their highest level since 2021, while net interest income rose 10% year over year to $25.6 billion. Meanwhile, Goldman Sachs raised the price target on the bank to $418 from $411 and kept a ‘Buy’ rating on the shares after its Q2 earnings beat, as per TheFly. JPM stock has gained more than 5% so far this year as retail sentiment improved from ‘bullish’ to ‘extremely bullish’ over 24 hours. BAC stock also climbed to a record high of $61.21 on Tuesday, driven by Q2 results that demonstrated a strong investment banking pipeline amid growing AI demand. The bank reported revenue of $31.6 billion, ahead of analyst estimates of $30.7 billion. Meanwhile, earnings per share (EPS) came in at $1.21, beating expectations of $1.13 EPS. Investment banking revenue climbed 50% year-over-year, with sales and trading revenue rising 30%. A surge of more than 70% in equities trading was the standout performer, contributing to one of the bank's best quarters in recent years. "We still have very strong pipelines in investment banking. The IPOs and deals are still getting done, and very strong interest in doing transactions,” CEO Brian Moynihan told CNBC in an interview. "The AI buildout still has a lot of debt funding and other funding required, so it's a very good environment." Meanwhile, Jefferies raised the price target on Bank of America to $75 from $70 and kept a ‘Buy’ rating on the shares after a "strong quarter," as per TheFly. BAC stock has gained more than 8% so far this year as retail sentiment improved from ‘neutral’ to ‘bullish’ over 24 hours. For updates and corrections, email newsroom[at]stocktwits[dot]com. Lucid stock faced one of the most turbulent trading sessions in its history on Tuesday, plummeting to an intraday record low of $2.37 after restructuring speculation triggered a dramatic sell-off in the luxury electric vehicle maker’s shares. The steep decline followed reports that restructuring adviser AlixPartners was reviewing options for the company, including possibilities that investors interpreted as potential bankruptcy or a private-market transaction. Lucid moved quickly to deny the claims, saying the bankruptcy-related speculation was “completely false.” The company said AlixPartners was assisting with operational improvements, including cost management, manufacturing efficiency and supply-chain efforts rather than preparing for insolvency proceedings. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around the stock jumped to ‘extremely bullish’ from ‘bearish’ territory the previous day. Oracle stock fell to a one-year low of $127.83 as investors questioned the financial burden of its aggressive expansion of artificial intelligence infrastructure. The company’s stock has declined 33% over the past month as concerns about spending, financing needs, and customer concentration have overshadowed optimism about its large cloud business. Oracle has a huge backlog of cloud orders, but the company is taking on more debt to build the data centers needed to complete those contracts. A major factor weighing on Oracle has been a downgrade from S&P Global, which lowered the company’s credit rating to BBB-, only one level above non-investment-grade status. The agency highlighted concerns about Oracle’s reliance on large customers, including OpenAI, which represents a large portion of its remaining performance obligations. Retail sentiment around the stock remained in ‘extremely bullish’ territory. Hertz Global stock fell to a six-year low of $1.75 as investors reacted to falling used-vehicle prices, heavy debt obligations and weakening financial conditions. Hertz recently pursued a $350 million convertible note offering to strengthen liquidity and slashed its adjusted second-quarter EBITDA outlook to between $50 million and $80 million. The company also reported higher fleet depreciation costs, adding pressure to its recovery efforts. Retail sentiment around the stock remained in ‘bullish’ territory. U.S. stock futures edged higher in the overnight session late Tuesday as softer-than-expected inflation data boosted technology stocks and eased rate hike concerns, overshadowing escalating tensions between the U.S. and Iran. Meanwhile, strong quarterly results from top banks on Tuesday reinforced market confidence in a solid earnings season. Dow futures were up 0.05%, S&P 500 futures climbed 0.18%, and Nasdaq-100 futures climbed 0.61% at 10:20 PM EDT. Among ETFs tracking benchmark indexes, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY), the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (DIA) and the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) were trading higher with sentiment in the ‘bullish’ territory. The iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF (TLT) was down 0.13% amid ‘extremely bearish’ sentiment. All three benchmark indexes closed higher on Tuesday, with the Nasdaq leading the decline, climbing nearly 1% higher at close. The S&P 500 was up 0.38%, while the Dow closed marginally higher, up 0.02%. The strongest boost for U.S. markets on Tuesday came from lower-than-expected June inflation. According to data from the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS), the Consumer Price Index (CPI) climbed 3.5% year-on-year, below market expectations. Meanwhile, core inflation came in at 2.6%, with prices declining 0.4% from the previous month, the largest monthly drop since May 2020. Lower energy costs drove the decline in headline inflation, with the energy index falling 5.7% in June. The softer inflation figures lowered expectations for a rate hike from the Federal Reserve. According to the CME's FedWatch tool, the probability of a rate hike at the July meeting fell to 15.5%, down from 41.7% a day earlier. Mohamed El-Erian, Chief Economic Advisor at Allianz, said on Tuesday that the lower inflation figures “should help temper what had become an excessively hawkish market tilt to the monetary policy outlook.” However, he warned that the softer print “won't fully resolve the debate over the forward-looking relevance of these numbers.” However, markets reacted positively to the lower inflation figures, with chipmaking stocks such as Nvidia Corp. (NVDA) and Micron Technology (MU) surging at close. Additionally, Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh testified before Congress on Tuesday, telling lawmakers that he expects the inflationary surge that has defined the past five years to fade into history. Economist Peter Schiff said in a post on X on Tuesday that “The only way regime change at the Fed will reduce inflation is if we also get regime change in Congress and the White House. Monetary and fiscal policy have worked hand in glove to create the inflation that plagues the economy. Ending it requires huge cuts to government spending.” Meanwhile, shares of U.S. banks surged on Tuesday after they reported second-quarter (Q2) results. Goldman Sachs (GS) led the climb, surging 9% at close after it reported record Q2 results. JPMorgan Chase (JPM) and Bank of America (BAC) also surged about 2% each following their Q2 prints. Shares of Rocket Lab (RKLB) rebounded after a six-session losing streak on Tuesday as CEO Peter Beck highlighted the company as one of the few proven commercial launch providers, calling SpaceX a “friendly rival” and noting that Rocket Lab emerged from a field of more than 100 failed challengers. RKLB stock jumped nearly 3% on Tuesday, with shares also up nearly 2% overnight. In a recent BBC interview, Beck said commercial launch remains exceptionally difficult despite billions of dollars in investment. “Despite billions of dollars and over 100 companies trying, there has actually only been two companies to pop out the other end,” with a regular and reliable launch service, he said, in a discussion that also touched on Rocket Lab’s rivalry with SpaceX. “Launch and a commercial company doing launch still remains extremely rare,” Beck added. Beck called SpaceX a “friendly rival” and said space companies often compete for one contract before working together on another: “You can be competing tooth and tail for a particular contract” and later team up to deliver it, he said. Rocket Lab can also benefit when rivals win as it supplies components such as reaction wheels, star trackers and solar panels.” “We can go head to head with a traditional space prime and then lose,” Beck said. “And then the next day, there’s a purchase order.” Beck called Rocket Lab an end-to-end space company spanning satellites, launch and services from orbit: “We build satellites, we launch them on our rockets and we provide services from space,” he said. Pointing to SpaceX’s Falcon 9 and Starlink model, Beck added: “They’re able to do all those things. And we’re able to do those too.” William Blair analyst Louie DiPalma recently named Rocket Lab and Blue Origin among the strongest challengers to SpaceX, though he said SpaceX still holds more than 90% of the launch market. Rocket Lab is advancing its competitive vertical integration strategy through its $8 billion acquisition of Iridium Communications, which would add a global network, spectrum, and recurring satellite service revenue. The company recently completed a full-duration burn of its Archimedes Vacuum engine, an important step toward the first flight of its reusable Neutron rocket. Rocket Lab said it was “critical preparation for Neutron’s first flight.” Beck has told Stocktwits earlier that Rocket Lab is “pushing very hard” to launch Neutron by the fourth quarter of 2026, while cautioning that the challenge is not merely reaching orbit but proving the rocket can return and be reused. “If we just had to go up, it’s super easy, we’d be in orbit by now,” he previously said. Rocket Lab also completed the U.S. Space Force’s Victus Haze mission, launching 16 hours and 42 minutes after receiving notice and completing spacecraft commissioning and proximity operations ahead of schedule. The company supplied the launch vehicle, spacecraft and orbital operations under one contract, offering a practical demonstration of the integrated model Beck outlined in the interview. Shares of top software companies, including ServiceNow and Salesforce, fell on Tuesday after IBM reported preliminary quarterly results showing acute weakness in its software business and said clients were shifting spending to AI servers faster than anticipated. ServiceNow stock declined 5.8%, while Adobe and Salesforce’s shares dropped 4.3% and 2.1%, respectively. Software heavyweight Microsoft closed 1.6% lower as well. The group edged higher in overnight trading, led by Microsoft, which rose 0.4%. "In the last few ⁠weeks of June, we saw clients shift their quarterly capex spend toward servers, storage, and memory purchases to secure supply-constrained infrastructure ahead of ​expected price increases," CEO Arvind Krishna said in a letter to investors. "While we anticipated some supply-chain related impact in our expectations, we did not anticipate ​the magnitude of the capex reprioritization," Krishna said, adding that the company “faltered” and "numerous large deals" had failed to close as expected. IBM said the weakness was largely in its mainframe business, which sells high-end enterprise computers and related software that power mission-critical workloads, including processing massive volumes of transactions for banks, governments, airlines, and retailers. It also noted that businesses were prioritizing cybersecurity due to recent advances in AI, including the release of Anthropic’s powerful Mythos technology. IBM expects second-quarter revenue to rise 1% to $17.2 billion, with 5% growth in its software business and a 7% decline in its infrastructure business. The bottom-line figures were rather concerning, with the gross profit margin expected to drop by 100 basis points to 57.7%. IBM shares dropped a record 25.2% on Tuesday. The company will issue the full quarterly report on July 22. The comments intensified concerns about AI-driven disruption across the software industry, fears that have been building for months and weighing on software stocks. Names such as Adobe, Salesforce, and Intuit have been among the hardest-hit tech stocks this year, prompting investors to debate whether the selloff has gone too far. (GFUZ) made history on Monday, becoming the first pure-play nuclear fusion energy company to trade on a major public stock exchange. In an exclusive interview with Stocktwits, CEO Greg Twinney argued that fusion is not just a cleaner alternative to fission but is a fundamentally larger market opportunity. GFUZ stock surged 21% on its debut, added over 25% on Tuesday, and was trading about 2.5% lower in the overnight session. The Vancouver-based company, backed by Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, among others, went public through a SPAC merger with Spring Valley Acquisition Corp. III, which provided General Fusion with approximately $150 million in cash. Earlier, Twinney told the Wall Street Journal that the funding is sufficient to meet the scientific milestones required by its demonstration machine. The listing arrives at a pivotal moment. Surging electricity demand driven by the AI boom, the global spread of electrification, and the energy appetite of large-scale computing has renewed urgency around new sources of firm, clean power. Fusion has attracted growing investment and government attention as a potential long-term answer. According to the Financial Times, the number of private fusion companies has more than doubled over the past five years, intensifying competition at a time when the technology is still roughly a decade from commercialization. General Fusion is targeting its first commercial plant around 2035. Twinney's bull case for fusion starts with what it doesn't produce. Unlike fission, fusion does not generate long-lived radioactive waste, does not use fuels that could be weaponized, and carries no risk of a meltdown. "Fusion is just inherently safe. We're not needing to engineer safety into it in the same way that you need to with fission," he told Stocktwits. "When fusion fails, it kind of just fails safely and there's not really any fallout from that." That safety profile has a direct commercial implication: regulators around the world are moving to govern fusion "in a much lighter way" than conventional nuclear, Twinney said, which he believes creates the potential to site fusion plants closer to population centers and industrial demand. That's a significant advantage over fission, which requires remote, heavily secured facilities. "We get all the benefits that fission can provide without the downsides," he said. There's another significant advantage. Fusion reactors primarily use deuterium, which can be extracted from seawater and is "massively abundant." The other component, tritium, is rarer in nature but can be bred through the interaction of a neutron and lithium. Fission, by contrast, relies on uranium and other finite sources. "The overall market size because of the safety profile and the abundance of fuel in fusion is much bigger than fission," Twinney said. While advanced nuclear companies such as Oklo Inc. (OKLO) and NuScale Power Corp. (SMR) are often thought of as being closer to commercialization than fusion technology, Twinney said that the gap may not be as large as investors assume. While the road to commercialization for fusion technology has its challenges, including achieving reactor durability, tritium fuel breeding, economic viability, and the ability to efficiently extract and convert fusion energy into electricity, he argues small modular reactor (SMR) timelines also struggle with regulatory hurdles that can make timelines less predictable than they appear today. "I know that the timelines for SMRs, which can be very unpredictable due to regulations and those types of things, [are] probably not that different," he said. According to Twinney, the combination of abundant fuel supplies and a lighter regulatory framework could ultimately enable fusion to scale faster than conventional nuclear technologies once commercial viability has been demonstrated. However, Twinney does not view fusion and fission as mutually exclusive technologies. "They will be complementing each other," he said. "And I think that fusion kind of rounds out the nuclear circle if you think about it that way," he added. When asked about criticism from former Commonwealth Fusion Systems CTO Dan Brunner, who, in a recent interview with the Financial Times, said General Fusion's commercialization timeline was "very hard to believe," Twinney said the company’s timelines were based on real experimental results from its Lawson Machine 26. The machine is designed to demonstrate that plasma can be heated through mechanical compression rather than superconducting magnets or high-powered lasers, he said, adding that the company's early results validated the operating principles behind its MTF approach that are “not based on fiction or papers being written.” The timelines “are based on our real results from machines that we have built and operated and then eventually written papers on. But those are real results papers, not theoretical papers,” he said. Twinney also emphasized that General Fusion's approach could offer a cost advantage over many competing technologies. While many other fusion developers rely on expensive superconducting magnets, high-powered lasers, or advanced materials that have yet to be proven at commercial scale, General Fusion's Magnetized Target Fusion (MTF) system uses mechanical compression and a liquid-lithium wall that can protect reactor components from neutron damage, help with breeding tritium fuel, and absorbing fusion energy as heat that can be converted into electricity using conventional steam turbines. In an earlier interview with Stocktwits, Chief Strategy Officer Megan Wilson had also pointed to the economic advantages of MTF, which eliminate the need for expensive magnets, targets, lasers, or exotic, not-yet-invented materials. The technology also eliminates the need for frequent replacement of components damaged by neutron exposure, she had said. “Our plants are designed to be cost-competitive compared to coal, steam, and natural gas,” she had said then. “They are expected to deliver four times as much energy per unit of fuel as fission, without long-lived radioactive waste, positioning them as the superior nuclear technology for sustainable growth.” By avoiding costly magnets and lasers and using existing industrial technologies, Twinney said he believes General Fusion has a clearer path to building an economically viable power plant, as the company’s design has from the beginning aimed to avoid the major barriers to commercializing fusion. "What we are trying to do at General Fusion, and our power plant design from the beginning, has been we want to avoid the major barriers to commercializing fusion. Not just demonstrate a bunch of fusion, but actually avoid the barriers to commercializing it," he said. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around GFUZ stock is ‘bullish’ amid ‘high’ message volumes. title: Goldman vs. Citigroup: Which Bank Stock Is the Better Buy Now? - The Globe and Mail
content: The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc.GS and Citigroup, Inc. C have long been pillars of the Wall Street heavyweights. Goldman is sharpening its focus on high-margin businesses, such as investment banking, trading and wealth management, while Citigroup is executing a sweeping restructuring aimed at simplifying its global footprint and improving profitability. With interest rates, capital markets activity and economic conditions continuing to shape the banking landscape, investors are asking a key question: which stock offers the stronger opportunity for now? Let us take a closer look and evaluate the potential of each bank. Goldman has long maintained a leading position in mergers and acquisitions, trading, and capital markets. Under CEO David Solomon, the company has undertaken a deliberate transformation to exit non-core consumer banking operations and concentrate resources on businesses wherein it holds clear competitive advantages, particularly investment banking (IB), trading, and asset and wealth management (AWM). Goldman has also been actively reshaping its portfolio through targeted acquisitions and divestitures. This month, GS entered an agreement to acquire LCN Capital Partners, which will strengthen its AWM business by adding a specialized platform focused on sale-leaseback, build-to-suit and triple-net-lease investments. The company has also agreed to acquire NEOS Investments, further expanding its presence in options-based ETFs. In April 2026, Goldman acquired Innovator Capital Management, enhancing its active ETF capabilities and supporting its broader strategy of building durable, fee-based revenues through diversified asset and wealth management offerings. During the same month, it completed the divestiture of its Polish asset management business, Goldman Sachs TFI, to ING Bank Slaski, further streamlining its operations. Collectively, these initiatives align with Goldman’s multi-year strategy to focus on institutional and wealth-led businesses, expand recurring fee revenues and reduce earnings volatility associated with non-core activities. Artificial intelligence (AI) is emerging as another important driver of efficiency and growth for Goldman. The firm is deploying AI across trading, investment banking, asset management and internal operations to enhance productivity, improve client service and generate greater operating leverage. Over time, these investments could strengthen Goldman’s data-driven capabilities, improve margins and support growth in higher-fee businesses. GS is also expanding aggressively in private markets. Its Asset Management unit aims to increase private credit assets to $300 billion by 2029 while broadening its presence across Europe, the U.K. and Asia. Together, these initiatives should strengthen Goldman’s alternative asset management franchise, diversify fee-based revenues and enhance the durability of its long-term earnings. Citigroup, by contrast, is far more sweeping. Under CEO Jane Fraser, the company is advancing its multi-year strategy to streamline operations and focus on its core businesses. Since announcing plans in April 2021 to exit consumer banking in 14 markets across Asia and EMEA, the company has completed exits in nine countries. Citigroup has moved closer to completing its multi-year exit from non-core international consumer banking. The sale of the Polish consumer business in June 2026 marked the final international consumer divestiture apart from remaining wind-downs of Banamex. The company also sold an additional 22.6% stake in Banamex in the second quarter after selling 25% in late 2025. The remaining Banamex deconsolidation and IPO are planned for early 2027, with management expecting the transaction to free up $5 billion in capital. These efforts are designed to free resources for faster-growing businesses, such as wealth management and investment banking. C expects revenues to see a 4-5% compound annual growth rate through 2026 and is targeting a 10-11% return on tangible common equity. Cost-cutting remains another major pillar of Citigroup’s growth strategy. As part of its restructuring program, the company remains on track to eliminate 20,000 positions by the end of 2026. Its total headcount declined to 219,000 as of June 30, 2026, from 230,000 a year earlier. In the first half of 2026, the bank incurred more than $800 million in severance costs, reflecting upfront investments to achieve sustainable operating efficiencies. Beyond workforce optimization, management is driving efficiency through process simplification, platform consolidation and increased automation, reducing manual touchpoints across operations. At the same time, the company continues to invest in technology and artificial intelligence to strengthen operational resilience, improve productivity and support revenue growth. To accelerate these initiatives, Citigroup plans to invest an incremental $5 billion between 2026 and 2028, with spending focused on technology modernization, marketing, front-office talent and branch renovations. Driven by such initiatives, C expects to generate $2-$2.5 billion in annualized cost savings by 2026. The company targets a full-year efficiency ratio of 60%. Citigroup is also expanding deeper into private markets and alternative investments through partnerships with major asset managers. In recent years, the bank has launched private credit and customized portfolio initiatives with BlackRock, Carlyle Group and Apollo Global Management to diversify revenue streams and strengthen client engagement. Over the past year, shares of Goldman and Citigroup have risen 38.4% and 37.6%, respectively, compared with the industry’s growth of 22%. In terms of valuation, Goldman is currently trading at a 12-month forward price-to-earnings (P/E) of 14.58X. Meanwhile, Citigroup’s stock is trading at a 12-month forward P/E of 10.68X. C is trading at a discount compared with the industry average of 13.97X. However, the GS stock is trading at a premium. C and GS reward their shareholders handsomely.  Following the Federal Reserve’s 2026 stress test, GS increased its quarterly common stock dividend by 11% to $5 per share beginning in the third quarter of 2026. Similarly, Citigroup announced a 12% quarterly dividend increase beginning in the third quarter, subject to board approval. Including dividends, C’s total return over the past five years has been 115.6% compared with Goldman’s average of 183.6% The Zacks Consensus Estimate for GS’s 2026 and 2027 earnings indicates increases of 34.2% and 4.9%, respectively. Over the past month, earnings estimates for both years have been revised upward. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for C’s 2026 and 2027 earnings indicates 40.5% and 15.5% growth, respectively. Over the past month, the earnings estimate for 2026 has been unchanged, while that for 2027 has been revised upward. Both Goldman and Citigroup have favorable growth catalysts, but the risk-reward profile currently tilts more convincingly toward Goldman. This is also consistent with their Zacks rankings, with Goldman sporting a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) compared with Citigroup’s Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). You can see the complete list of today’s Zacks #1 Rank stocks here. The key differentiator is earnings visibility. Goldman is benefiting from stronger estimate revisions for both 2026 and 2027, reflecting improving expectations for investment banking, trading and asset and wealth management. Its strategic shift toward fee-generating businesses, particularly alternatives and wealth management, should also make its revenue mix more durable over time. At the same time, investments in AI and technology could support productivity gains and operating leverage as revenues expand. Citigroup offers a different investment case. Its restructuring, cost reductions and relatively inexpensive valuation create meaningful upside potential if management delivers on its profitability targets. However, a larger portion of that upside remains dependent on successful execution of its transformation, including expense discipline, business simplification and improved returns. This makes Citigroup’s earnings trajectory comparatively more execution-sensitive. Valuation is the principal argument in Citigroup’s favor, as Goldman commands a higher multiple. Yet the premium appears warranted, given GS’ stronger franchise positioning, better earnings momentum and more visible growth drivers. In contrast, Citigroup’s valuation discount partly reflects the uncertainty surrounding the timing and magnitude of returns from its restructuring. Thus, while Citigroup remains an attractive turnaround story, Goldman offers a stronger combination of earnings momentum, business quality and growth visibility. title: GS Engineering & Construction partners with Carlo Ratti on climate-resilient housing research for Xi apartments - 헤럴드경제
content: GS Engineering & Construction announced Tuesday that it has conducted joint research on "future climate-resilient residential concepts" with CRA (Carlo Ratti Associati), the architecture and innovation design firm led by architect and professor Carlo Ratti. The research focused on analyzing the impact of climate change on residential environments using data-driven methods, with the goal of developing new solutions to protect residents' health and safety as well as their housing assets. The two firms jointly analyzed domestic and international residential environments based on data covering key climate variables — including heavy rainfall, extreme heat and fine dust — combining CRA's data analysis and sensor-based design capabilities with GS Engineering & Construction's housing construction and operations expertise. Through the collaboration, GS Engineering & Construction developed a range of future-oriented residential concepts designed to address climate challenges such as heavy rainfall, extreme heat and fine dust. The company plans to conduct pilot tests to verify the technical feasibility and effectiveness of the findings, which are currently at the conceptual stage. Technologies that pass verification will then be applied sequentially to Xi apartments, taking into account the conditions and characteristics of each project site. "This joint research is significant in that it analyzed the impact of the climate crisis on residential environments through a data-driven approach and explored proactive countermeasures," a GS Engineering & Construction official said. "We will continue to pursue research and technology verification to create a next-generation residential environment where Xi residents can live safely and comfortably even amid climate change." Meanwhile, Professor Ratti is the director of the Senseable City Lab at MIT and a founding partner of CRA. He is widely recognized as a leading expert in "responsive design" — an approach that integrates data and sensor technology into urban and architectural settings to respond to environmental changes in real time. Among CRA's notable sustainable buildings are Capitalspring in Singapore and the Jianmu Tower in Shenzhen. His signature works also include the Digital Water Pavilion in Zaragoza, Spain.

title: This 300-HP Lexus Sleeper Matched BMW Muscle Without The German Repair Bills - HotCars
content: Subscribe to the HotCars newsletter to never miss an update By the late 1990s, the luxury sports sedan had evolved into one of the automotive industry's fiercest battlegrounds. Premium automakers were no longer competing solely on refinement, prestige, or comfort—straight-line performance had become just as important. Yet impressive acceleration figures alone weren't enough to win enthusiast approval. Reputation increasingly depended on something less tangible: how a car made its driver feel. Amid that landscape, one Japanese luxury sedan quietly produced performance numbers comparable to the benchmark BMW 540i, yet never earned the same reputation. Its greatest disadvantage wasn't found beneath the hood or within its chassis, but somewhere far less mechanical. We've updated the article with more details on the evolution of this Lexus luxury sedan. By the time the E39-generation BMW 540i arrived,     BMW had already established itself as the benchmark for building sports sedans that balanced luxury with genuine driver involvement. The 540i refined that formula further by combining a smooth, naturally aspirated V8 with a chassis that felt equally comfortable on a winding back road and a long-distance highway journey. It wasn't the fastest executive sedan of its era, nor the most powerful, but it delivered an experience that felt complete in a way few rivals managed. Much of that reputation stemmed from BMW's decision to offer the 540i with a six-speed manual transmission. At a time when luxury manufacturers were increasingly steering buyers toward sophisticated automatic gearboxes, BMW continued to cater to enthusiasts who valued direct mechanical engagement above outright convenience. The manual-equipped 540i became more than just another drivetrain option—it became central to the car's identity and helped cement its status as the driver's choice within the segment. That timing proved significant because enthusiast culture increasingly equated three pedals with authenticity. Automotive publications praised manual transmissions for the greater sense of involvement they provided, while buyers often viewed them as proof that a manufacturer genuinely prioritized the driving experience. Automatic transmissions had become smoother, more intelligent, and, in many situations, equally capable, but public perception hadn't evolved at the same pace. As a result, any rival hoping to challenge the BMW faced an obstacle extending well beyond measurable performance. Matching its acceleration or handling would not automatically earn the same respect if enthusiasts believed the driving experience itself was compromised. It was against this backdrop that another luxury manufacturer quietly pursued a fundamentally different vision for the modern performance sedan. While much of the segment increasingly embraced the formula that had made German performance sedans so desirable, one manufacturer chose not to chase driver involvement in exactly the same way. Instead of building a car that demanded constant interaction, its engineers focused on delivering effortless performance, exceptional refinement, and the kind of long-term durability that had already become a defining strength of the brand. The objective wasn't to imitate the benchmark—it was to prove there was another path to building a genuinely capable luxury performance sedan. That philosophy shaped the development of a new rear-wheel-drive executive sedan that represented a significant departure from its predecessor. Engineers strengthened the chassis, refined the suspension, sharpened steering response, and improved overall body control, but resisted sacrificing ride quality simply to create a harsher, more aggressive character. The goal remained balance rather than extremity, ensuring the car retained the comfort expected of a premium luxury sedan while becoming noticeably more rewarding to drive. The same thinking extended beneath the hood. Rather than chasing peak horsepower figures alone, engineers concentrated on creating a V8 that delivered broad, effortless torque, exceptional smoothness, and dependable performance over hundreds of thousands of miles. Variable Valve Timing with intelligence (VVT-i) broadened the engine's operating range, while careful calibration prioritized immediate real-world response instead of requiring constant high-rev driving to access meaningful performance. The result reflected an engineering philosophy that valued usable speed over dramatic theater. That approach ultimately produced a luxury sedan capable of matching the segment's established benchmark where objective performance was concerned—even if it arrived there through an entirely different philosophy. That sedan was the Lexus GS 400, introduced as the flagship performance model of the second-generation GS lineup. Rather than attempting to replicate BMW's character, Lexus developed the GS 400 to demonstrate that effortless refinement and genuine performance could coexist without compromise. It wasn't designed to become a track-focused sports sedan or a luxury car with a larger engine. Instead, it embodied Lexus's belief that engineering sophistication could deliver competitive performance while remaining unmistakably Lexus. Power came from a revised 4.0-liter 1UZ-FE V8 equipped with VVT-i, producing 300 horsepower and 310 lb-ft of torque. Paired exclusively with a five-speed electronically controlled automatic transmission driving the rear wheels, the GS 400 recorded 0–60 mph times ranging from approximately 5.7 to 6.0 seconds in contemporary road tests, depending on the publication. Those figures placed it directly alongside the BMW 540i and Mercedes-Benz E420/E430, proving that Lexus had achieved genuine parity where straight-line performance was concerned. The engine's character mattered just as much as its headline figures. With roughly 80 percent of its peak torque available from just 1,800 rpm, the revised 1UZ-FE delivered immediate, seamless acceleration across almost the entire rev range. Rather than encouraging drivers to chase redlines, it produced effortless thrust whether pulling away from traffic lights, merging onto a highway, or overtaking slower vehicles. That broad torque delivery perfectly reflected Lexus' grand touring philosophy, making the GS 400 feel consistently responsive without demanding constant driver effort. The industry's recognition of the 1UZ-FE reinforced that engineering achievement. The V8 earned repeated praise for combining refinement, performance, and durability, including recognition through Ward's 10 Best Engines program during the GS 400's production period. It demonstrated that Lexus hadn't simply built a reliable luxury engine—it had created one of the most sophisticated V8 powerplants of its era. On paper and on the road, the GS 400 had achieved exactly what it set out to do: produce performance capable of running with the BMW 540i through engineering rather than imitation. Despite matching the     BMW 540i in outright performance, the GS 400 never achieved the same standing among driving enthusiasts. The reason had little to do with horsepower, acceleration, or chassis capability. Instead, it came down to a single product decision that shaped public perception from the moment the car arrived in showrooms. Unlike the BMW 540i, which offered buyers the option of a six-speed manual transmission, the GS 400 was available exclusively with a five-speed electronically controlled automatic. Lexus engineered the transmission to prioritize smoothness and refinement, while its E-Shift manual mode allowed drivers to select gears sequentially. For everyday driving, it was quick, unobtrusive, and well matched to the V8's broad torque curve. But to enthusiasts accustomed to equating manual gearboxes with driver involvement, it wasn't enough. Period road tests reflected that contrast. Reviewers consistently praised the GS 400's composure, effortless power delivery, and remarkable refinement, often acknowledging that it could match or closely trail the BMW in objective performance testing. Yet when discussions turned to driver engagement, the conversation almost inevitably returned to the BMW's manual transmission. The ability to choose gears manually with a clutch pedal created a stronger emotional connection, even if it offered little measurable advantage in day-to-day performance. That distinction ultimately shaped how both cars were remembered. The BMW became the enthusiast's benchmark because it delivered not only speed, but also a level of interaction that buyers associated with a true driver's car. The Lexus, meanwhile, was viewed as the more mature and refined alternative—a car that achieved similar results through engineering sophistication rather than mechanical theater. In hindsight, its reputation was influenced less by what it could do than by what it chose not to offer. The second-generation Lexus GS was a major leap over the first-generation car when it debuted in 1998. For the first time in the U.S.-market GS, buyers could get a V8, and the GS 400's 4.0-liter 1UZ-FE arrived with VVT-i, helping transform the sedan into a much more capable performance machine. The new platform was also substantially stiffer and more sophisticated than its predecessor. But the luxury sedan segment was moving fast. An escalating technology race among European rivals, combined with tightening emissions requirements, pushed Lexus to rethink the formula just three years into the second-generation GS's run. In 2001, the GS received a significant mid-cycle refresh. The exterior received a cleaned-up grille, revised lighting, larger exhaust tips, and fresh six-spoke alloy wheels. The cabin received an equally important technology upgrade, with available DVD navigation, standard audio controls on the steering wheel, a compass, improved audio equipment, and new trim details. Lexus also added standard side-curtain airbags and other safety upgrades, pushing the GS further into premium-sedan territory. Yet the biggest change was hiding beneath the bodywork. Lexus replaced the 4.0-liter V8 with a larger engine, bringing the GS 400 nameplate to an end and ushering the performance sedan into its next chapter as the     GS 430. The GS 430's 4.3-liter 3UZ-FE wasn't a clean-sheet engine. Lexus took the proven 1UZ-FE and stretched its displacement the easy way: the stroke stayed at 82.5 mm, while the bore grew from 87.5 to 91.0 mm. The result was 4,293 cc versus 3,969 cc, giving the facelifted sedan more low- and mid-range muscle while helping the V8 satisfy evolving emissions requirements. The headline power figure stayed at 300 hp, but torque rose from 310 to 325 lb-ft, giving the GS 430 stronger low- and mid-range shove. Lexus also refined the engine's control systems, retaining VVT-i while optimizing VVT-i, ACIS and ETCS-i and revising the intake, exhaust, ignition and emissions hardware for a cleaner, smoother and more efficient power delivery. That doesn't mean enthusiasts automatically prefer the newer V8, as some still choose the 1UZ. Its smaller bore and thicker cylinder liners give high-output builders more material to work with, while the 3UZ's larger bore and thinner liners leave less room for aggressive builds. The GS 400's ETCS-i also retained a physical accelerator cable as part of its mechanical fail-safe system, a touch that still appeals to tuners who prefer a more mechanical connection to the throttle. Viewed through a modern lens, the GS 400's philosophy appears surprisingly forward-thinking. Today's high-performance luxury sedans are almost exclusively equipped with sophisticated automatic transmissions, while smooth, effortless torque delivery has become a defining characteristic of the segment. The qualities that once led some enthusiasts to dismiss the Lexus have since become accepted as the industry standard. Its naturally aspirated     1UZ-FE V8 has also earned a reputation for exceptional durability, with numerous examples covering high mileage while retaining the refinement that made the engine so impressive when new. Combined with conservative styling, solid build quality, and a well-balanced rear-wheel-drive platform, the GS 400 has become increasingly appreciated by enthusiasts seeking an understated performance sedan that can still be driven and enjoyed without constant mechanical attention. Perhaps more importantly, time has shifted the conversation away from what the GS 400 lacked and toward what it accomplished. Rather than attempting to imitate BMW's formula, Lexus proved there was another way to build a compelling performance sedan—one that prioritized seamless power delivery, engineering refinement, and everyday usability without sacrificing genuine pace. That philosophy may not have generated the same enthusiast mythology as the manual-equipped 540i, but it produced a car that has aged with remarkable dignity. The GS 400 was never remembered as loudly as its German rival, yet history suggests it deserved greater recognition. It demonstrated that matching the benchmark didn't require copying it, and that intelligent engineering could be just as effective as chasing the traditional enthusiast playbook. Its legacy is therefore defined not by the transmission it never offered, but by how convincingly it proved there was more than one route to building a great V8 sport sedan. Currently, examples trade in the range of $7,000 to $11,500 on the used market. Sources: Lexus Pressroom and Heritage, Toyota Global We want to hear from you.
